results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 63 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (including p21 and p48 inside the architecture, p51 opening In Practice, p62-p63 in the close); the five callouts are unmatched framing. The outliner's two-ideas mark on p19 is judged under one_controlling_idea_per_paragraph.

results.draft_locus: The Tracking Plan: The Schema Nobody Can Recall ¶5
results.quote: Two design rules follow from the table.
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit as two ideas, and it carries two: the fields of the common envelope, and two collection rules (facts server-side, impressions compacted not dropped) that the draft itself says follow from the core-events table, not from the envelope. The spec's controlling idea for p19 bundles both, so the draft cannot split them without a spec change (one paragraph for the envelope, one for the two rules).
Every unit advances its declared supporting claims (S1-S6) or is declared framing (intro context, roadmap, scene, hand-off); no unit drifts from the thesis.

Each table is introduced and read: scene definitions (p06, read by p07-p08), six outputs (p11), three kinds of data (p13-p14), core events (p19), layers (p23-p24), quality controls (p48), storage options (p27 recommendation, p28), ownership matrix (p32), definition card (p35), replay (p38), legal regimes (p45), trade-offs (p54 lead-in states the choosing rule), verticals (p56). Quotations (Dehghani, Adevinta 2024, Aurelia 2025, Armbrust et al.) and statistics (Artemis, OLX uplift, Meilleurs Agents, Scout24, logging cost) are each followed by what they show.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary, e.g. 'This chapter takes the opposite route' (problem_solution), 'Owning the word starts with knowing what the platform is for' (cause_effect), 'The tracking plan governs one input; the reference architecture below receives all of them' (sequence), 'Validation at the gate is the first of several quality controls' (elaboration), 'The contacts data product needs a definition its owner publishes', 'Priya's team tested the definition in April, before the forum approved it' (time), 'Pro data products serve a brand's own customers ... data that crosses from one brand to another' (contrast), 'Veldmark's answer to three warehouses and three contacts' (problem_solution), 'Preventing those failures is a Chief Architect's work', 'Henrik's question was answered by contracts'. Boundaries that open under a subheading (storage, data products, verticals) are carried by the subheading and the preceding unit's pointer.

Organising principle: both readers describe a problem scene, then the platform in the order the data travels (purpose, tracking plan, architecture, data products, governed metrics, pro data, cross-brand sharing, freshness and cost), then the Veldmark design and the book's standard judging sections; this agrees with the declared prerequisite_order with problem_solution and grouping. Names both readers flagged as unintroduced (Common Ground, Yardstick, Veldmark ID, Safe Deal, Valuo, Sven Lindqvist, Listing event contract v1, Tradeyard's countries, the billable lead, strangler, DAC7, DSA) are on the audience's already_knows list or owned by earlier chapters, so they are not counted as lost-thread points for the target reader.

results.quote: Three of its layers hold **data products**, datasets a named team owns and publishes; their owners follow the rule in the next section.
results.finding: Reader A: 'this paragraph defines data products, data contracts and the metrics layer in passing and refers to "the rule in the next section." Each term is then defined again in full later ... so I read three definitions twice.' Both readers propose a different order (A: governed metrics before the architecture; B: data products before the architecture). The density comes from the spec's choice to put the architecture before the sections that define its terms and to gloss them here, so the order itself causes the re-read.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'The opening paragraph of the Architecture section (line 125) ... All three terms are defined again properly later ... I had to re-read this paragraph.'

results.quote: Adevinta Benelux's metric monitoring, Artemis (described under governed metrics), is the same
results.finding: Reader A: 'Line 150: "Artemis (described under governed metrics)." A forward reference to a tool I know nothing about yet.' The spec's controlling idea (quality is cheapest at the source, a control at each layer) does not need Artemis here; the prose cites an example the reader meets two sections later.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: '"Adevinta Benelux's metric monitoring, Artemis (described under governed metrics)" (line 150): this is a forward reference ... the point did not land.'

results.draft_locus: Governed Metrics: One Definition of a Contact ¶5
results.quote: The week began on Monday 8 March, the day after Femke listed her bike, so the team replayed the bike's first 24 hours with it.
results.finding: Reader A: 'Line 227 needed a re-read ... the Essen Volkswagen Golf, listed ... on 14 April, sits outside the replayed March week, and it was "replayed in April" in a test that was itself run "in April." The two timelines blur.' The timing (a March week that excludes the bike's listing day, a Golf listed in April added to the same replay, and 'none excluded') is fixed by the spec's controlling idea for p37, so the prose cannot simplify it without a spec change.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'The replay paragraph (line 227) ... I re-read the paragraph twice to settle which events fall in which time window.'

results.quote: Access policy settles what data may be used; keeping the platform useful and affordable is the remaining work
results.finding: Reader B: 'Freshness and Cost: the stated link is "the remaining work", which is weak. The reason for its position is somewhat unclear. It reads like a leftover.' Both readers propose moving its content (B: freshness into the architecture, cost into In Practice; A: Veldmark's cost figures into this section). The section has no prerequisite tie to cross-brand sharing, so the difficulty comes from its position in the spec's order.
results.corroborated_by: Reader A, item 2: 'Freshness and Cost: ... The link is clear, but it reads like leftover topics.'

Every does_not_know term is given at or before its first substantive use: data platform (p09), tracking plan (p15), common envelope (p19), data contract, data product and metrics layer (glossed in p23, defined in p25, p29, p33), governed metric (framed in p02, defined p33), qualified contact (card, p34), pro data product (p41), lakehouse and open table formats (p27), medallion (p24, as bronze/silver/gold), data mesh (p29), quarantine tables (p25), ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and GDPR purpose limitation (p20). Terms the flow readers found unexplained (Veldmark names and cast, Yardstick, Valuo, Safe Deal, Veldmark ID, strangler, DAC7, DSA, the billable lead) are on already_knows or owned by earlier chapters (bounded-contexts, marketplace-regulation, event-driven-listings, monetization-models).

Opens with a direct, disputable statement ('Most marketplace data platforms are built backwards'), bridges to the topic, names the four contracts and puts technology after them, states the neighbours and gives a roadmap; no dictionary, throat-clearing or 'in this chapter we will' opening.
The close does not restate sections or open with 'in conclusion'; it synthesises (contracts, not an engine), gives a course of action and hands off to experimentation.

p62 states what the contracts achieved (Femke's bike counts 13 wherever it is read; facts, not only data) and the first step; p63 answers the so-what: comparable measurement lets the group ask whether a change caused an effect.
'Henrik's question was answered by contracts' and 'the platform holds facts, not only data' call back to the scene's board question and the opening's 'a great deal of data and very few facts'.

The cold intro reader reconstructed every roadmap promise in order (board question, purpose, tracking plan, architecture with quality controls, data products, governed metrics, pro data, cross-brand sharing, freshness and cost, Common Ground design, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions) and the evidence kinds; the body keeps that order.

From the opening alone the reader named the subject (warehouses with conflicting contact definitions; tracking plan, governed metrics, federated ownership, purpose-bound access), all sections in order, and the evidence (Adevinta, OLX, Scout24, AutoScout24, Vinted, Zalando; data-mesh and lakehouse literature; EU law; fictional Veldmark). Its note that consent has no separate roadmap step does not change the predicted order.

Using only the chapter, the reader built qualified_contact v1.0 with an owning domain and steward, written definition, version, counted once per buyer and listing at server-side delivery with fraud excluded by the 72-hour restatement (the listing counts 13), legacy definitions labeled side by side for a quarter, dealer reports and billing reading the same product and switched with the board pack; and refused the subsidiary request through hard isolation as access policy (no federation, only contract-named aggregates leave, audit log readable by the independent reviewer).
